test_title: PYST 10: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - English (Held On: 15th Sep 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question: A sentence is given in direct speech. Choose the option that expresses it correctly in indirect speech: I said, “He will arrive by noon.”

options.text: I said that he would arrive by noon.
I said he shall arrive by noon.
I said that he will arrive by noon.
I said that he would be arriving by noon.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** I said that he would arrive by noon.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"will" becomes "would"**
 
 
• Future tense "will" is changed to "would" to match the past reporting verb "said."
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Direct: "I said" remains unchanged in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Sentence Structure:**
 
 
• Direct speech: "He will arrive by noon."
 
• Indirect speech: "I said that he would arrive by noon."
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• Conjunction "that" is added to connect the reporting clause and the reported speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I said that he would arrive by noon."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "I said he shall arrive by noon."
 
 
• Incorrect usage of "shall" instead of "would" or "will."
 
• Does not match indirect speech rules for tense conversion.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "I said that he will arrive by noon."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "will" should change to "would" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "I said that he would be arriving by noon."
 
 
• While grammatically correct, this option alters the meaning slightly by using the continuous tense "would be arriving" instead of "would arrive."
 
 
</ul
